cosy-lesson.title: "Study hard what interests you the most in the most undisciplined, irreverent and original manner possible.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Undisciplined – ignoring strict rules, timetables, or formal academic structures; free-form.

p.em: Example: Feynman loved an undisciplined approach to learning, focusing only on what captured his mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Irreverent – disrespectful of rigid rules, traditional conventions, or serious academic authorities.

p.em: Example: His irreverent jokes in the physics laboratory shocked some of the senior professors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Original – created personally; completely fresh, unique, and not copied from others.

p.em: Example: Instead of using textbook formulas, he created his own original visual diagrams.

cosy-blockquote.p: Interest – a feeling of wanting to learn about, focus on, or pay attention to a specific topic.

p.em: Example: If a lesson doesn't capture your natural interest, studying becomes a stressful chore.

cosy-blockquote.p: Syllabus – the official list of topics, subjects, and books in a formal school course.

p.em: Example: Feynman often ignored the school syllabus to explore random scientific side-quests.

cosy-blockquote.p: Authority – the official power or right to give orders, make rules, and demand obedience.

p.em: Example: Feynman refused to bow to academic authority, questioning every established theory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Explore – to investigate, study, or search through a new subject or concept thoroughly.

p.em: Example: As an autodidact, she loved to explore coding languages completely by herself.

cosy-blockquote.p: Convention – a traditional, generally accepted way of behaving or doing something.

p.em: Example: Challenging social convention is essential if you want to discover original ideas.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rebel – a person who resists or stands up against rigid rules, customs, or authorities.

p.em: Example: In the quiet world of physics, Feynman was a colorful rebel who played bongo drums.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passion – an extremely strong, intense enthusiasm or excitement for a subject or activity.

p.em: Example: His deep passion for biology was born during random walks in the forest with his father.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What does Richard Feynman mean when he tells us to study in an undisciplined manner?
★ Have you ever achieved a personal breakthrough by studying in an undisciplined way?

Why is pursuing seemingly irrelevant side-quests crucial for a creative career?
★ What is the most unusual, seemingly irrelevant skill or topic you have researched?

How does cultivating an original style of thought protect us from standard expectations?
★ Do you have a unique working method that you consider highly original?

How does academic convention kill the natural, playful interest of young students?
★ When was the last time you felt a genuine, deep interest in a school syllabus?

Should students be given complete autonomy to ignore the school syllabus and study what they love?
★ Did you ever feel restricted by your high school syllabus?

Why do many traditional institutions fear unorthodox methods of teaching and evaluation?
★ Have you ever challenged a strict authority figure in your career or studies?

How can we combine creative, playful chaos with the absolute rigor required for scientific accuracy?
★ When did a strict rule or hard discipline teach you a valuable lesson?

How does a successful autodidact manage to synthesize knowledge from multiple areas?
★ What is the most difficult skill you had to explore completely by yourself?

Why is a self-directed learner often seen as a rebel by traditional groups?
★ Do you consider yourself a bit of a rebel when it comes to your hobbies?

How can we find the quiet mental space to fuel our passion in a hyper-distracted world?
★ What is your single biggest creative passion in life right now?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is Feynman's "undisciplined manner" most effective? Rank them: - 🗣️ Learning a Language Watching foreign comedies and speaking in a messy, undisciplined manner without looking at any grammar books. - 🧪 Doing Scientific Research Playing with bongo drums and thinking of irrelevant visual diagrams to synthesize physics laws. - 🚀 Building computer code Ignoring all corporate authority and coding an original, unorthodox project late at night. - 🎨 Learning original art Ignoring every textbook convention and painting completely based on your chaotic inner passion.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, standard school systems will completely ban standard syllabuses, allowing kids to learn in an undisciplined manner. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you send your children to an undisciplined school that has zero rules?

AI tutors will eventually design customized programs fully based on a student's random, irrelevant side-interests. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you trust an AI agent to decide which irrelevant topics you should explore next?

In a highly automated world, holding an original style of creative thought will be the only safe human skill. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is one highly original hobby or interest you hope to protect over the next decade?

Future societies will prioritize absolute individual autonomy over any academic or professional conventions. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you hope future kids will have much more cognitive autonomy than today's children?

In the coming decades, choosing not to conform and studying in an unorthodox way will be seen as highly positive. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where every academic convention is decided by smart algorithms?

As AI manages all analytical jobs, physical classrooms will disappear, giving learners complete freedom to explore their hobbies. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you had unlimited free time, which complex subject would you choose to explore?

Future corporate cultures will completely eliminate the authority of managers, turning workers into self-guided rebels. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you enjoy working as a creative rebel without any strict corporate authority?

Biometric systems will allow us to measure a person's raw passion, replacing standard credentials. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you hope that future hiring is driven by a candidate's actual passion rather than grades?

A future world governed fully by logic will leave no space left for the quiet mystery of individual interest. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to exercise greater personal interest right now?

Academic rigor will become fully obsolete as artificial neural networks take over all scientific tasks. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your rigor, would you still value human science?

ul.li: Incorrect: I studies in an undisciplined way → Correct: I study in an undisciplined manner ((First-person verb agreement, use 'manner' to match original quote))
Incorrect: He discussed about the syllabus → Correct: He discussed the syllabus (('Discuss' is transitive and does not take 'about'))
Incorrect: I am agree with Feynman → Correct: I agree with Feynman (('Agree' is a verb, not an adjective))
